alarm.screen.description: Press the button below to cycle through the different types of alarms available. When you've found the one you want, click the 'Done' button at the bottom. Supply a redstone pulse (on/off signal) to any side of the box to sound the alarm.
alarm.screen.name: Alarm %s
death.attack.assortedtech.laser.player: %1$s got zapped by a laser whilst trying to escape %2$s
death.attack.assortedtech.spike.player: %1$s walked into a spike whilst trying to escape %2$s
gps_sensor.screen.any_mobs: Any mob, or an id like zombie
gps_sensor.screen.any_players: Any player, or type a name
gps_sensor.screen.entries.empty.items: Nothing added, so any item counts.
gps_sensor.screen.entries.empty.mobs: Nothing added, so any mob counts.
gps_sensor.screen.entries.empty.players: Nothing added, so any player counts.
gps_sensor.screen.gps_hint: Put a GPS here to watch the position it stored
gps_sensor.screen.help.items: Press + or Enter to add it to the list, or click an item on the slot instead. The sensor watches for anything on the list. Start with # for an item tag, like #minecraft:logs.
gps_sensor.screen.help.mobs: Press + or Enter to add it to the list. The sensor watches for anything on it. Start with # for an entity tag, like #minecraft:undead.
gps_sensor.screen.help.players: Press + or Enter to add the name to the list. The sensor watches for anyone on it.
gps_sensor.screen.item_add_hint: Click an item on the slot to add it to the list
gps_sensor.screen.item_change_hint: Click another item to swap it, or click empty handed to clear it
gps_sensor.screen.item_hint: Click an item on the slot
gps_sensor.screen.status.blocked: %s, %s, %s is solid, nothing can be there
gps_sensor.screen.status.other_dimension: The GPS's position is in another dimension
gps_sensor.screen.status.out_of_range: The position is more than %s blocks away
manual.assortedtech.chapter.bridges.acce: An acceleration bridge carries you along faster than walking. Useful for long crossings.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.bridges.deat: A death bridge looks like a trick bridge and hurts anything that touches the beam.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.bridges.grav: A gravity lift is a beam you step into rather than onto. The lift will push whatever is inside it the way it points.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.bridges.lase:
A bridge control shoots a beam when it is given redstone, and the beam is solid ground. It cannot be broken while it is lit, and it stops at the first block in the way.

Right click the control with a block to give the beam that block's texture, and shift right click with an empty hand to put it back.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.bridges.tric: A trick bridge is a laser bridge you fall straight through. It looks solid but definiitely is not.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.extruder.ext:
Right click it to fuel it, choose its direction and start/stop it. You can also punch it with an empty hand to start or stop it.

It will move in a straight line, mining whatever the material it is made out of can mine, and lays a block from its top slots behind itself at every step.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.extruder.mat:
An extruder is made from a pickaxe, shovel and axe of one material, and mines only what those tools can mine. There is one for every material that Assorted Core supports.

Upgraded extruders require an extruder of the previous level surrounded by its tools. Each level is faster, more efficient and has more inventory slots than the previous level.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.gravity.attr:
Powered, an attractor pulls everything within towards it.

The directional version only pulls on the face the cone points out of.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.gravity.boot: Wearing gravity boots, none of the blocks in this chapter move you at all.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.gravity.grav:
A gravitor lifts whatever is near it straight up while it is powered, and lets go the moment it stops. Whatever was in the air then falls the whole way.

The directional version only lifts on the face it points out of.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.gravity.repu:
A repulsor is an attractor run backwards. When powered, it pushes everything in range away.

The directional version pushes only out of the face it points.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.redstone.ala:
An alarm sounds while it has power, and goes on any face of a block. Right click it to pick which of the sounds it makes.

Wired to a sensor it becomes a doorbell, or something considerably less polite.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.redstone.fan:
A fan blows entities away from itself or pulls them towards it. Right click it to set the range and which mode is set.

Redstone turns a fan off rather than on, so it runs by default and a lever stops it.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.redstone.fli: A flip flop torch changes state each time it is powered and stays there. One button turns it on, the same button turns it off, which saves building the latch yourself.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.redstone.glo: A glowstone torch lights up when it is powered and goes dark when it is not, the way a redstone lamp does, but you can still walk through it like any torch.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.sensors.gps: Right click a block with a GPS to store the space in front of it. Sneak and use it in the air to forget it.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.sensors.gps_:
A GPS sensor watches the position a GPS stored rather than the space in front of it, so it can sit behind a wall or under the floor. Right click it and put the GPS in the slot at the top right.

You can open the GUI and choose between players, mobs and items, and narrow it to one player, one kind of mob or one item.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.sensors.sens:
A sensor watches the space in front of it and gives out redstone while something it cares about is there. A light on the face shows when it has seen one.

Which things it cares about is decided by what it is made of, so the recipe is the setting. The next page lists them.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.sensors.trig:
Wood sees everything, including dropped items and arrows. Stone sees anything alive. Iron sees only players.

Mossy cobblestone sees hostile mobs, cobweb sees spiders and their kin, netherrack sees what belongs in the Nether, and end stone sees what belongs in the End.

Gold sees dropped items, emerald sees villagers and wandering traders, prismarine sees what swims, feather sees what flies, and a hay bale sees tamed pets.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.sensors.upgr:
The upgraded GPS sensor can be farther away and supports an adjusteable range.

The upgraded GPS sensor supports a list of 6 entries each as well as supporting entity and item tags now.

Start an entry with # to use a tag, like #minecraft:undead for every undead mob or #minecraft:logs for every log.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.spikes.mater: What a spike is made of decides how hard it hits. We support many Vanilla materials and every material Assorted Core adds.
manual.assortedtech.chapter.spikes.spike:
A spike goes on any face of a block, floor, wall or ceiling, and hurts whatever touches it when powered.

An unpowered spike is flush against the ground and does nothing.
manual.assortedtech.description: Laser bridges, gravity, sensors, spikes and additional redstone fun.
manual.assortedtech.title: Assorted Tech
